{{Quote|One Jenet's trash is another Jenet's treasure.|Old saying|<ref name="GG4a" />}}
The '''Jenets''', or '''Jenet''', were a [[Species/Legends|species]] of [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]], [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoid]] [[Rodent/Legends|rodents]], best known for their exceptional memories and scavenger nature. Other species often regarded Jenets as ugly and quarrelsome. They had [[Color/Legends|pink]] skin, red [[Eye/Legends|eyes]], and wiry [[Hair/Legends|fur]], which grew sparsely on the body but more thickly on their heads. Their prominent whiskers twitched as they spoke. As adaptations to aid scavenging, they could digest almost any form of organic matter, and could rely upon keen eyesight, hearing, and smell. The species were excellent runners, climbers, and swimmers, and their flexible bodies allowed them to squeeze through openings as narrow as twelve [[Centimeter/Legends|centimeters]] by disjointing their long [[Limb/Legends|limbs]] and separating their [[Bone/Legends|cranial plates]]. Jenet [[Reproduction/Legends|reproductive]] biology encouraged rapid population growth, as both gestation and maturation occurred rapidly in comparison to those processes in many other species.

Originally from the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Garban]] in the [[Tau Sakar system]], the Jenets evolved into cunning survivalists who systematically drove into extinction those species that [[Hunting/Legends|preyed]] upon them, an event they remembered as the [[Great Conquest]]. The exception was the [[danchaf]], a clever arboreal species whose presence in Garban's [[Tree/Legends|forests]] prevented the Jenets from fully dominating such areas. As their technology progressed, the Jenets colonized the six other habitable planets that orbited [[Tau Sakar]] to ameliorate conditions on their increasingly overcrowded [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]]. Their communities across the [[Star system/Legends|system]] were distinguished by the species' tortuous bureaucracy, made up of Jenets whose jobs were simply to commit to memory as many facts about their fellows as possible. Jenet eidetic recall influenced social relations, as a Jenet's name contained a long list of [[Gender/Legends|his or her]] deeds and accomplishments and informed others of that individual's status in Jenet society. The rulers of the species were the [[Council of 127]] and the [[Premiere (Jenet)|premier]]. Jenet populations maintained [[Community Heap]]s, cooperatively owned landfills replete with scavenged and discarded items. With the ascension of [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Galactic Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] and the [[Declaration of a New Order|institution]] of the [[New Order/Legends|New Order]], the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] found the Jenets to be useful as [[Slavery/Legends|slaves]], because the rodents' high reproductive rate allowed their masters to pay little attention to the detrimental effects of poor labor and living conditions.

Those Jenets who migrated beyond the Tau Sakar system often found employment in fields that made use of their infallible memories, such as [[Politics/Legends|government]], administration, and business. For example, a Jenet named [[Losh]] worked in the [[civil service divisions]] on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] and helped [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Gregar Typho/Legends|Gregar Typho]] of [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]] investigate the [[Death/Legends|death]] of [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]]. However, other Jenets ventured into [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy's]] criminal element. The [[Invisible Shell]], for instance, was a crime ring operated by a clan of Jenets on the planet [[Pavo Prime/Legends|Pavo Prime]] under the leadership of a male named [[Lorimar Lebauer]]. The species' ability to remember even minor details of things they had seen or heard also made them excellent [[Spy/Legends|spies]]. Despite their mistreatment by the Empire, few Jenets supported the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]] or joined its successor state, the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]]. After the Republic transitioned to the [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances|Galactic Alliance]], at least some Jenets allied with the government; two such were [[Thorsh]], a Jenet espionage agent during the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]], and [[Reeqo Swen]], a Jenet [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]]-in-[[Jedi training/Legends|training]].

==Biology and appearance==
{{Quote|You must have a hard head.|Han Solo, to Thorsh|<ref name="TUF">''[[The New Jedi Order: The Unifying Force]]''</ref>}}
[[File:Jenet_2.jpg|left|thumb|upright|Some Jenets were quite bulky.]]
Jenets, or Jenet,<ref name="Plurality">''[[Galaxy Guide 4: Alien Races]]'' and [[Galaxy Guide 4: Alien Races (Second Edition)|Second Edition]] use "Jenet" for both the singular and plural name of the species, while ''[[Ultimate Alien Anthology]]'' uses "Jenets" as the plural form.</ref> were a [[Species/Legends|species]] regarded as unattractive<ref name="GG4b">[[Galaxy Guide 4: Alien Races (Second Edition)|''Galaxy Guide 4: Alien Races'', Second Edition]]</ref>&mdash;if not repulsive&mdash;by [[Human/Legends|Humans]].<ref name="TTWS">{{Hyperspace|url=hyperspace/member/fiction/f20051028/index.html|text=The Trouble with Squibs}}</ref> They were [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Rodent/Legends|rodents]]<ref name="UAA" /> who stood between 1.4 and 1.6 [[Meter/Legends|meters]] tall.<ref name="height" /> Although a few individuals exhibited a highly muscled or corpulent physique,<ref name="TTWS" /><ref name="UAA" /> the average Jenet had a gaunt build characterized by long, thin [[Limb/Legends|limbs]].<ref name="EGAS" /> Jenet locomotion involved a bipedal gait<ref name="GG4b" /> whereby they walked on their toes, with the long, wedge-shaped feet<ref name="TUF" /> jutting upward at an angle. Their forelimbs terminated in four attenuated fingers and an opposable thumb,<ref name="EGAS" /> and their hindpaws in four elongated toes. All of these digits ended in sharp claws.<ref name="UAA" /> Although Jenet physiology made them adept at running, jumping, swimming and climbing,<ref name="EGAS" /> their general form of movement was to scurry from place to place.<ref name="Inf" /> They also exhibited extreme flexibility: a Jenet could fit through an opening as small as twelve [[Centimeter/Legends|centimeters]] across by dislocating his or her limbs and separating the individual [[Bone/Legends|bones]] of the cranium to squeeze through.<ref name="EGAS" />

A Jenet's pale,<ref name="GG4a" /> oily,<ref name="TTWS" /> pink skin<ref name="CSWE II 155">{{CSWECite|II|155|Jenet}}.</ref> was covered in coarse,<ref name="TUF" /> thin [[Hair/Legends|fur]].<ref name="CSWE II 155" /> It grew more thickly on the top of the head, where a mass of hair of a different [[Color/Legends|color]] from the main coat might have manifested. Fur colors ranged from white<ref name="GG4b" /> or gray<ref name="TJP" /> to red.<ref name="A" /> Some individuals sported a short beard as well.<ref name="TUF" />

The rounded<ref name="TTWS" /> Jenet muzzle could grow quite long,<ref name="SP">{{JournalCite|11|Spare Parts (short story)}}</ref> terminating in a wet [[Nose/Legends|nose]]<ref name="Tempest">''[[Legacy of the Force: Tempest]]''</ref> surrounded by stiff whiskers<ref name="UAA" /> that grew to a length equal to the smallest opening through which a Jenet could fit.<ref name="GG4a" /> The beings had a keen sense of smell, developed to help them find food. A cleft upper lip lay below the nostrils,<ref name="EGAS" /> only partially covering a pronounced set<ref name="Tempest" /><ref name="CNIISoS">''[[Coruscant Nights II: Street of Shadows]]''</ref> of sharp,<ref name="Tempest" /> yellowish [[Tooth/Legends|teeth]]. Jenets had small, red [[Eye/Legends|eyes]]<ref name="UAA" /> set under thick brow ridges. The rodents were noted for their keen eyesight, another food-finding adaptation;<ref name="EGAS" /> they could see well even in low-light conditions.<ref name="UAA" /> Their pointed [[Ear/Legends|ears]] lay flat against the head, providing most members of the species acute hearing<ref name="GG4b" />&mdash;although not all Jenet shared this trait.<ref name="TTWS" />

Jenets were [[Diet/Legends|omnivorous]]. They were able to digest virtually any organic matter,<ref name="EGAS" /> and their diet ranged from wild [[Fruit/Legends|fruit]] to [[Death/Legends|necrotic]] flesh.<ref name="GG4a" /> At least some members of the species slept with their arms and legs held tight to the body and the muzzle nestled near the hindlimbs.<ref name="Tempest" />

Jenets had two [[Gender/Legends|sexes]] and [[Reproduction/Legends|reproduced]] sexually. Pregnant females carried their offspring in the womb for ninety standard days before bearing a litter of typically four to six [[Youngling/Legends|young]]. Jenets matured rapidly; they learned to walk by two [[Standard month/Legends|months]] of age<ref name="EGAS" /> and entered adolescence at four [[Standard year/Legends|standard years]]. Jenets reached sexual maturity at nine and had a life expectancy of seventy standard years.<ref name="UAA" /> Jenets were particularly fecund, so that a female rarely went more than a standard year before giving birth to another litter.<ref name="GG4a" /><ref name="GG4b" />

==Society and culture==
{{Quote|Say, do you remember Als Somda?|A Jenet|<ref name="GG4a" />}}
[[File:Jenetgg4.jpg|right|thumb|upright|Despite their fur, Jenets wore clothing as a marker of status.]]
Jenets were temperamental and obsessed with trivialities,<ref name="EGAS" /><ref name="GG4b" /> which led many other species to regard them as irksome and obnoxious.<ref name="UAA" /> Despite their dominance over their [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] both [[Politics/Legends|politically]] and technologically,<ref name="GG4a" /> Jenets were unabashed scavengers by nature. They never discarded anything: whatever they acquired was kept in their homes or in large piles in their community's warrens. These [[Community Heap]]s, filled with broken tools, leftover food, empty containers, and the like, were common property, and Jenets enjoyed rummaging through them to find items of use.<ref name="GG4b" /> Although they were omnivores, they did not [[Hunting/Legends|hunt]] or raise animals; rather, they ate only meat they found from an animal that had already died. The species practiced animal husbandry to ensure that the wild creatures of their worlds did not overpopulate. The Jenets themselves had to contend with creatures that might try to eat them, so they kept an ear out for such attacks while working. The sentient rodents were adept at fleeing in an emergency, running and leaping to safety.<ref name="GG4a" />

A notable Jenet trait was their extraordinarily accurate and detailed memories;<ref name="CSWE II 155" /> members of the species never forgot even the most trivial datum.<ref name="GG4b" /> One manifestation of this characteristic was a tradition of ballad [[Music/Legends|singing]] about ancient heroes, poems beloved by the rodents but considered doggerel by non-Jenets.<ref name="COTG">''[[Creatures of the Galaxy]]''</ref> This infallible memory also meant that Jenets never forgot slights and insults, and therefore could hold grudges indefinitely. In Jenet society, rumors and reputation were of paramount importance: Jenets could hold actions against even people whom they had never met, based merely on hearsay.<ref name="GG4b" /> Jenets cared little for what other species considered tact,<ref name="UAA" /> so they were not shy about airing these opinions and grievances in public.<ref name="GG4a" /> Since they could easily recall any bit of information about another person, Jenets freely insulted each other, even when among close friends and family. Exchanges of excoriation were so common as to be a form of greeting,<ref name="CNIISoS" /> since an upbraided Jenet could usually recall some embarrassing fact about his or her interlocutor. Jenets took pride in being denigrated, for it proved they had gained enough notoriety to be worth the effort. However, few non-Jenets found such treatment enjoyable. Members of other species usually considered the Jenets' temperament to be argumentative, pedantic, dull, and uncouth.<ref name="GG4b" /><ref name="CSWE II 155" /> Some non-Jenets even accursed the rodents of fabricating memories so as to influence others. These widely held beliefs meant that many species simply chose to avoid Jenets when possible.<ref name="GG4a" /> Nevertheless, the Jenets had no tolerance for ignorance or duplicity.<ref name="UAA" /> Members of the Jenet species, in particular, are known to enjoy keeping [[yeomet]]s as pets.<ref name="COTG" />

The Jenets had access to all aspects of [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] technology, including [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]]-capable [[Starship/Legends|starships]].<ref name="GG4b" /> Nevertheless, their homeworld of [[Garban]] boasted only a limited-service [[Spaceport/Legends|spaceport]].<ref name="FTG">{{JournalCite|10|A Free-Trader's Guide to the Planets}}</ref> Most Jenets had a healthy work ethic,<ref name="CNIISoS" /> and their obsessive attention to detail made them useful employees.<ref name="UAA" /> However, they tended not to learn technological skills<ref name="EGAS" /> and preferred to automate as much of their production as possible in lieu of mass labor.<ref name="GG4b" /> Members of the species particularly hated working as [[Miner/Legends|miners]].<ref name="GG4a" /> Despite their fur, Jenets tended to wear clothing. The style of this varied with the individual; some males preferred loose-fitting tunics with trousers,<ref name="EGAS" /><ref name="GG4a" /> while others sported a more militaristic look, with button-down jacket and epaulettes.<ref name="UAA" /> Each member of a group led by [[Ludlo Lebauer]] wore an elaborate and expensive [[noron]] doublet and tunic suit with a [[Blaster/Legends|blaster]] sidearm. Some females wore backless blouses with shorts that reached the knees and were slitted up the hip, a look considered provocative by male members of the species. Others had [[clingsilk]] skirts.<ref name="TTWS" />

===Language===
{{Quote|I am Losh. I have seen pictures of your homeworld. Unsightly, water-ridden place.''"<br />"''Perhaps so, but for sheer global repulsiveness little can compare to Garban.''"<br />"''You are familiar with Jenet society?''"<br />"''With the basics. As a security officer I have to know galactic protocol. It wouldn't do to greet someone from the Tau Sakar system, much less Garban itself, with a flowery compliment.''"<br />"''Indeed it would not.|Losh and Gregar Typho|<ref name="CNIISoS" />}}
The species' native [[Language/Legends|language]], also called [[Jenet (language)|Jenet]],<ref name="UAA" /> consisted of soft, short bursts<ref name="CNIISoS" /> of high-pitched chittering, squeaking, squealing, and barking.<ref name="UAA" /> Different sounds indicated different concepts; one type of squeak showed approval, for example,<ref name="CNIISoS" /> and a certain sniff showed scorn.<ref name="TUF" /> Due to the species' long memories, there was no written form of the language; things that other species might write down were simply committed to memory. Some Jenets learned [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Basic]], but this was not a species-wide skill.<ref name="UAA" /> Rodent-like mannerisms accompanied Jenet speech. A Jenet's nose,<ref name="GG4a" /> whiskers,<ref name="CNIISoS" /> and snout<ref name="TUF" /> could twitch and jerk<ref name="CNIISoS" /> to convey emotions such as amusement, condescension,<ref name="TUQ">''[[Dark Nest II: The Unseen Queen]]''</ref> concern,<ref name="Tempest" /> disgust,<ref name="Inf">''[[Legacy of the Force: Inferno]]''</ref> or unease.<ref name="Tempest" /> This was accompanied by expressive movements of the ears,<ref name="SP" /> eyes, lips,<ref name="TTWS" /> and head.<ref name="Inf" /> Jenets laughed to show that they found something funny.<ref name="TTWS" /> Others developed habits of caressing<ref name="CNIISoS" /> or pulling on their whiskers while communicating.<ref name="Inf" /> Males and females flirted with one another.<ref name="TTWS" />

At their core, Jenet names generally consisted of one or two segments, such as Shan'Gredor Chirr't Ferr, Rhet H'rrr, and Ch'irrk Felt.<ref name="COTG" /> However, over [[Time/Legends|time]], Jenets expected others to recognize them with longer appellations that recounted their accomplishments and exploits. For example, a Jenet named Channik might eventually be known as Channik Who Built a [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]] and Flew to [[Ryloth/Legends|Ryloth]], a member of the species called Lezarn might be called Lezarn Who Deals in [[Spice/Legends|Spice]], while a third named Rish might come to be known as Rish Who Slew Vahgar the Drunken [[Houk/Legends|Houk]].<ref name="UAA" /> When Jenets were introduced to each other, a complete record of their achievements was given as part of their names. With this information, Jenets could tell where another Jenet was placed in their complex social hierarchy. Accomplishments that increased status required two other Jenets as witnesses. To avoid conflicts of interest, Jenets were never allowed to introduce themselves. Pairs of Jenets could work together for years without knowing each other's name, simply because a third Jenet acquainted with them both was unavailable.<ref name="EGAS" /> This did not entirely prevent Jenets from dishonesty, as they frequently exaggerated the accomplishments of their friends and downplayed the exploits of Jenets they disliked. This complex system of requesting and giving names sometimes led to confusion when Jenets dealt with members of other species, whom the rodents might have expected to also follow this custom.<ref name="GG4b" />

===Government and demographics===
[[File:Planet03-SWR.png|left|thumb|The Jenet Premier ruled the species' homeworld, Garban.]]
The Jenets lived on Garban and six other habitable [[Planet/Legends|planets]] in the [[Tau Sakar system]]<ref name="SWE" /> of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]].<ref name="CSWE I 322">{{CSWECite|I|322|Garban}}.</ref> They were divided into clans<ref name="TTWS" /> and tended to live only among their own kind. Female Jenets had little role in society other than to bear young.<ref name="GG4b" /> Due to their rapid reproduction, however, their enclaves could easily lead to all members being related to one another and the introduction of genetic defects from inbreeding. Jenets thus set up ties with other Jenet groups to exchange children&mdash;whom they called "sub-adults"<ref name="SP" />&mdash;and thus increase the gene pool.<ref name="GG4b" /> Jenet children could walk and scavenge their own meals at two months of age.<ref name="GG4a" /> Jenets put their children in [[school]]s to educate them.<ref name="SP" />

The Jenets shared Garban with the [[danchaf]], or [[Tree/Legends|tree]] goblins, a creature they held to be highly intelligent but which many [[Scientist/Legends|scientists]] considered non-sentient. Still, the Jenets claimed that the danchaf were simply too intelligent&mdash;and dangerous&mdash;to be observed by scientists in the field. Jenet oral histories spoke of the danchaf with great trepidation, and the Jenets avoided the tree goblin's forest habitat.<ref name="COTG" /> Instead, their communities were subterranean warrens dug deep into the surface of their worlds.<ref name="UAA" /> Such burrows were cramped and claustrophobic, but to Jenets, they were normal&mdash;although the conditions caused Jenets to misunderstand the importance of personal space to members of other species.<ref name="GG4b" /> Life in such enclosed spaces led to generalized acrophobia; Jenets much preferred subterranean environments to elevated ones.<ref name="UAA" /> They exhibited utmost cooperation with one another due to the exacting social stratification that their photographic memories afforded. Another practical application of their recitation of names and histories upon meeting one another was that when a Jenet heard the background of another Jenet, it allowed him or her to gauge whether the new acquaintance was a social superior or inferior, and thus whether or not he or she was worth dealing with. Despite the social stratification this system engendered and upheld, deeds were the ultimate determiner of status, so Jenet society allowed for social mobility.<ref name="GG4a" />

The Jenets were ruled by a [[Premiere (Jenet)|premier]]<ref name="EGAS" /> or premiere, assisted in his or her duties by the [[Council of 127]]. These positions were selected via an opaque process poorly understood among non-Jenets, although all members of the species knew who their rulers were based on the accomplishments listed in their names.<ref name="GG4b" /> The council oversaw a huge, byzantine bureaucracy, which they ran like a corporation.<ref name="UAA" /> The bureaucracy's job was to oversee resources and secure the homeland. Millions of Jenets served as functionaries in the government, their task to memorize details about as many other Jenets as they could. This information was then used to assign jobs, resolve disputes, and distribute resources. Group deposits of goods known as Community Heaps fell under the bureaucracy's administration.<ref name="GG4b" /> The prevalence of red tape in Jenet society meant that members of the species were seldom bothered by such matters even when dealing with the bureaucracies of other cultures.<ref name="UAA" />

==History==
{{Quote|Ch'irrk Felt's cry of battle rallied / Our hearts to the heroic slaughter, / When it was over, the dead were tallied; / Three cousins dead, one my daughter.<br />''"''My heart was rent, but the treasure was great, / Twenty goblins, whom we hate, / Lie dead upon the soggy earth, / So let us rejoice, and emerge with mirth!|Excerpt from ''The Ballad of Shan'Gredor''|<ref name="COTG" />}}
The Jenets evolved from rodent prey animals on Garban. Using the remains of ancient trash piles, [[Archaeology/Legends|archaeologists]] hypothesized that after the species had developed sentience, early Jenets lived in caves underground. They stayed in such cramped confines for much of their day, only stepping out to the surface to scavenge for food.<ref name="GG4b" /> Experts agreed that thousands of years before the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], ancient Jenets organized against their predators and began an onslaught against the species they had once feared.<ref name="UAA" /> Jenet legend revered this period, which they called the [[Great Conquest]], as a time of heroes and [[Soldier/Legends|warriors]], immortalized in epic poetry. According to such tales, the danchaf of Garban were once a sophisticated and cunning species who ruled Garban's woodlands in packs and prevented the Jenets from penetrating the forests. The Jenet rulers [[Chirr't Ferr]] and [[Rhet H'rrr]] formed [[Army/Legends|armies]] to drive back the danchaf hordes. H'rrr, according to legend, developed attacks to target camale danchaf&mdash;one of the species' four genders&mdash;and thus disturb the tree goblins' reproductive abilities. An epic titled ''[[The Ballad of Shan'Gredor]]'' told of the Jenet [[Ch'irrk Felt]], who created a giant trap of pots, pans, and bright [[phospowder]]; the noise and blinding lights dazzled the danchaf and allowed the Jenet soldiers to slay them. Although such wars were unsuccessful in eradicating the danchaf from the planet, legend claimed that the Jenet attacks forced the danchaf to devolve into a primitive state and allowed the Jenets to spread out and dominate Garban. With the exception of a [[Xenobiologist/Legends|xenobiologist]] named [[Xemlorn]], scientists dismissed any notion of a more sophisticated past for the danchaf, thus doubting the veracity of the Jenets' heroic tales. To the Jenets, however, the legends were key elements of oral history.<ref name="COTG" />

[[File:Danchaf.jpg|right|thumb|upright|Jenet lore told of the Great Conquest, a war in which the Jenets defeated the danchaf, or tree goblins, and claimed domain over the surface of Garban.]]
Jenet society came to be organized into clans and oriented around life in warrens. The Jenet bureaucracy developed, as did the positions of premier and the Council of 127. Jenets also learned to manage the animals on their world without resorting to widespread eradication. The species advanced technologically, eventually reaching [[Realspace/Legends|spaceflight]] by their own innovation or scavenging a [[Sublight engine/Legends|stardrive]] from another source.<ref name="EGAS" /><ref name="GG4a" />

Over time, Jenet fecundity and lack of predators caused the species to overpopulate Garban. The Jenets sent settlers to the other worlds of the Tau Sakar [[Star system/Legends|system]], where they found conditions very similar to those on Garban&mdash;a fact that led scholars to postulate that an unknown intelligence once [[Terraforming/Legends|terraformed]] the planets.<ref name="GG4b" /> The Jenets eventually founded colonies outside the Tau Sakar system as well,<ref name="UAA" /> and over time they reached technological parity with other advanced worlds in the [[Galaxy/Legends|galaxy]].<ref name="GG4b" /> Their system became part of the [[Abrion sector/Legends|Abrion sector]]<ref name="SWR">[[Star Wars: Rebellion (video game)|''Star Wars: Rebellion'']].</ref> in the Outer Rim Territories.<ref name="Atlas">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-essential-atlas-online-companion|text=''Star Wars: The Essential Atlas'' Online Companion|int=Star Wars: The Essential Atlas Online Companion}}.</ref>

The Jenets' spread to other worlds inevitably brought them into contact with pan-galactic government. During the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] took over the Tau Sakar system. Imperial [[sentientologist]] and propagandist [[Obo Rin]] included the Jenets in his ''[[Catalog of Intelligent Life in the Galaxy]]'', a project commissioned by [[Lord/Legends|Lord]] [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]] to detail those sentient species of most interest to the Empire.<ref name="GG4a" /> Rin claimed that the galactic regime protected the Jenets from marauding members of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]]; in exchange, the Jenets gladly served the [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] as laborers,<ref name="GG4b" /> mining [[Ore/Legends|ore]] from the planets of their home system.<ref name="CSWE I 322" /> In the Jenets' view, however, they were mere [[Slavery/Legends|slaves]], forced to live in labor camps<ref name="CSWE II 155" /> and undertake a task that they collectively deplored.<ref name="GG4a" /> The Empire found the Jenets to be useful workers on other planets as well due to their high reproductive rate, which rendered any worries about mortality levels moot. Accordingly, enslaved Jenets often operated in perilous work conditions. The Empire set up breeding facilities for the species in an effort to select for traits that increased their pacifist tendencies and compliance and decreased their intellects.<ref name="UAA" /> Jenets willing to fight back against the Empire were rare, and few members of the species joined the Rebel Alliance.<ref name="GG4b" />

After the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|collapse]] of the Empire in [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]], the Jenets still had to contend with the after-effects of a generation of Imperial breeding programs and enslavement. The species never joined the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]], the successor state of the Rebel Alliance, due to their preference for being among only their own kind,<ref name="UAA" /> although individual Jenets did serve in various capacities in the new government and its successor, the [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances]].<ref name="A" /> The [[Shi'ido]] [[Sentientologist|anthropologist]] [[Mammon Hoole]] included an entry on the Jenets in his publication ''[[The Essential Guide to Alien Species]]''.<ref name="EGAS" />

==Jenets in the galaxy==
{{Quote|The Jenet my servant Lotkha brought me &hellip; has proven profitable. I keep him present at all my meetings, and he remembers the proceedings in astounding detail. He watches for responses I cannot watch and reports them to me. Through him, I learn their weaknesses, their fears, and their needs. These Jenet make efficient, vindictive spies, who are judicial with the knowledge they retain.|Bwahl the Hutt, on his Jenet slave, "Jen"|<ref name="EGAS" />}}
[[File:TUF1_cover_JP.jpg|left|thumb|The Jenet Thorsh worked for the Galactic Alliance.]]
Jenets away from the Tau Sakar system preferred to live in Jenet-only colonies, isolated from any further integration with other species.<ref name="UAA" /> Due to their species' prolific reproductive rate, such an arrangement was easily achieved. However, to prevent inbreeding, even Jenet communities away from their home system maintained the tradition of swapping children with other groups to widen the available gene pool.<ref name="GG4b" /> The preference for other Jenets encouraged the species to travel in groups; when an outsider encountered a Jenet, he or she could expect other Jenets to be nearby.<ref name="UAA" /> The [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]] [[Alema Rar]] encountered two Jenets sleeping in a private chamber in the [[Coruscant Underworld/Legends|lower levels]] of [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] in [[40 ABY/Legends|40 ABY]], for example.<ref name="Tempest" />

For income, many Jenets capitalized on their memories to work as [[Administrator/Legends|administrators]], [[Bureaucrat/Legends|bureaucrats]], and [[Merchant/Legends|merchants]].<ref name="GG4b" /> For instance, in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], a middle-aged Jenet named [[Losh]] was employed at the headquarters of the [[civil service divisions]] on Coruscant. When a Human named [[Gregar Typho/Legends|Gregar Typho]] came looking for information about Human [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] Anakin Skywalker and the mysterious death of the Human [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]], his knowledge of Jenet customs endeared him to the bureaucrat and prompted Losh to set him on the correct trail.<ref name="CNIISoS" /> The Jenets had established an [[Jenet embassy|embassy]] to the [[Uvena system/Legends|Uvena system]], home of the [[Shistavanen/Legends|Shistavanen]] species, by the Galactic Civil War. During that period, the Shistavanens [[Yurdak Fav]] and [[Lak Sivrak/Legends|Lak Sivrak]] found their species' [[Alpha Premier]], [[Korta Sarc]], dead at the embassy.<ref name="AIR">''[[Alliance Intelligence Reports]]''</ref> Under the tyrannical regime of [[Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]], many Jenets in administrative positions were forced to work as slaves of the Empire.<ref name="GG4b" />

After the New Republic and its successor, the Galactic Federation of Free Alliance, rose to prominence, some Jenets found work for the latter government in bureaucratic and administrative occupations. During the [[Swarm War]], the Human [[Chief of State (Galactic Alliance)|Chief of State]] [[Cal Omas]] employed a Jenet personal assistant named [[Salla]] at [[Unity Green]];<ref name="TUQ" /> one of her tasks was to refuse to schedule meetings with individuals whom Omas did not wish to see.<ref name="TSW">''[[Dark Nest III: The Swarm War]]''.</ref> Other Jenets sided against the New Republic and Galactic Alliance; during the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]], a [[Unidentified Jenet Peace Brigade member|Jenet]] joined the [[Peace Brigade]], an organization that supported the invading [[Yuuzhan Vong]] and fought against the galactic government. He attacked the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] Knights [[Jaina Solo Fel|Jaina Solo]] and [[Lowbacca]] when they penetrated a bunker used by Peace Brigade members of the [[Ylesian Senate]] during a [[Battle of Yag'Dhul (29 ABY)|battle]] on the planet [[Ylesia/Legends|Ylesia]], but Solo dispatched him with a kick to the face.<ref name="Y">''[[The New Jedi Order: Ylesia]]''</ref> During the later [[Second Galactic Civil War]], the Human [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] and Galactic Alliance Chief of State [[Darth Caedus]] employed a Jenet administrative aide and [[Lieutenant/Legends|lieutenant]] named [[Orlopp]].<ref name="Tempest" /><ref name="Inf" />

[[File:OpunTols.jpg|right|thumb|upright|Tols Vengra worked for the crime lord Opun Mcgrrrr.]]
Other Jenets operated within the galactic underworld as criminals<ref name="GG4b" /> and [[Scoundrel/Legends|scoundrels]].<ref name="UAA" /> For instance, [[Tols Vengra]] had [[Cyborg/Legends|cyborg]] surgery to implant a [[Borg Construct Aj^6]] implant to enhance his memory even beyond Jenet standards. Despite earlier ambitions to enter his species' bureaucracy and serve in government, the surgery removed all desire to help others. Vengra eventually found work with [[Opun Mcgrrrr]], a Human [[Crime lord/Legends|crime lord]]. Vengra ascended to become Mcgrrrr's personal assistant, but in reality, the Jenet had control of most of the organization's affairs. Rather than challenge his nominal boss's leadership, however, Vengra siphoned off funds to prepare for his retirement at a later date. In [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]], Mcgrrr ordered Vengra to track down [[CZ-3/Legends|CZ-3]], a wayward [[CZ-series secretary/comm droid|CZ-series communications/business droid]] on the planet [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]]. The assignment brought Vengra into conflict with the [[Snivvian/Legends|Snivvian]] [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] [[Zutton/Legends|Snaggletooth]]&mdash;after the same droid for its owner, [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba Desilijic Tiure]]&mdash;and his brother [[Takeel/Legends|Takeel]] and brought about the destruction of the droid. Snaggletooth then used the droid's [[Photoreceptor/Legends|photoreceptor]] recording to show Vengra's involvement in the incident and thus implicate Mcgrrrr's organization.<ref name="SP" />

The Lebauer clan of Jenets was involved in the [[Gambling/Legends|gambling]] industry on the planet [[Pavo Prime/Legends|Pavo Prime]], with investments in the [[Seahorse Casino]] and ownership of the [[Pearl Island Casino]]. Jenets served the Pearl Island as clerks, overseers, security guards [[Bartender/Legends|bartenders]], porters, and pit bosses. However, these gaming interests were simply cover for the [[Invisible Shell]], a criminal organization run by [[Lorimar Lebauer]] and other elders of the clan; the various Jenets employed there were also trained as brawlers who could be called upon to defend the organization's interests if the need arose. After Lorimar Lebauer was arrested by the [[Vratix/Legends|Thyferrans]] for selling counterfeit [[Bacta/Legends|bacta]]&mdash;a product over which they controlled supply and distribution&mdash;Lebauer's organization fell under the nominal control of his nephew, [[Ludlo Lebauer]]. In [[8 ABY/Legends|8 ABY]], a New Republic delegation consisting of the Humans [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa Solo]] and [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]], the [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiee]] [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]], and the [[Protocol droid/Legends|protocol droid]] [[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]] visited Pavo Prime to bargain with Ludlo Lebauer for [[boasa]] statues from the planet [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]] that he had in his possession. Although Lebauer tried to squeeze the New Republic delegation for lucrative salvaging contracts, two other Jenets&mdash;whom Organa Solo dubbed [[Moonface]] and [[Tall]]&mdash;seemed more willing to part with the artwork. Organa Solo eventually offered to have Lorimar Lebauer freed from [[Prison/Legends|jail]] in exchange for the statues, something she knew Ludlo Lebauer did not want&mdash;but which he could not refuse without revealing his animosity for his [[Prisoner/Legends|imprisoned]] uncle. After a heated standoff with Lebauer and his assistant, a Jenet named [[Verm]], the Solos talked their way out of danger by revealing that they had recorded Ludlo Lebauer speaking favorably about his uncle's incarceration, and in exchange for burying that information, the younger Lebauer allowed the New Republic representatives to depart with the boasas.<ref name="TTWS" />

Eight Jenet guards protected a [[Onadax Droid Technologies headquarters|factory]] that manufactured [[Human replica droid]]s on the planet [[Onadax]] in [[28 ABY/Legends|28 ABY]]. When Jedi Knight Jaina Solo arrived there, she used [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] to [[Mind trick/Legends|cloud]] the guards' perception and pass herself off as a [[Mynock/Legends|mynock]]. When she later escaped, the perception had faded, and the Jenets tried to shoot her; nevertheless, she made it out of the compound.<ref name="ODT">{{InsiderCite|75|Or Die Trying}}</ref> [[Unidentified Jenet criminal|Another Jenet criminal]] received visitors in a [[Cantina/Legends|cantina]] near the [[Killik/Legends|Killik]] [[Lizil (Hive)|Lizil]] [[Lizil|nest]] in [[35 ABY/Legends|35 ABY]], during the [[Dark Nest Crisis]].<ref name="TJK">''[[Dark Nest I: The Joiner King]]''</ref> Other Jenets operated as [[Fringer/Legends|fringers]].<ref name="UAA" /> For instance, Jenets sometimes patronized the [[Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina/Legends|Mos Eisley Cantina]] on Tatooine; in [[5 ABY/Legends|5 ABY]], [[Zorba Desilijic Tiure|Zorba]] the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] learned that Leia Organa had [[Battle of the Great Pit of Carkoon|killed]] his son, Jabba, from [[Unidentified Jenet (Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina)|one]] of these Jenets.<ref name="ZTHR">''[[Zorba the Hutt's Revenge]]''</ref>

[[File:FaeCoven-TJP.png|left|thumb|Jedi Grand Master Fae Coven helped write ''The Jedi Path''.]]
Jenets made excellent [[Spy/Legends|spies]]. One, a slave who had been named "[[Jen (Jenet)|Jen]]" by his master, [[Bwahl]] the Hutt, observed the Hutt's meetings and remembered the goings on, thus providing Bwahl insight into details that the Hutt may have missed.<ref name="EGAS" /> The [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'lek]] [[Tavri]] caught a [[Unidentified Jenet spy|Jenet]] spying on him in a [[Mos Eisley/Legends|Mos Eisley]] [[Hangar/Legends|docking bay]] during the Galactic Civil War. Before Tavri could discover who the Jenet worked for, the spy went for a weapon, and Tavri was forced to kill him.<ref name="DT">{{JournalCite|3|Droid Trouble}}</ref> In [[29 ABY/Legends|29 ABY]], during the Yuuzhan Vong War, a Jenet named [[Thorsh]]&mdash;short for his full Jenet name&mdash;worked as a New Republic reconnaissance and espionage expert. He was [[Second Battle of Bilbringi|captured]] by the Yuuzhan Vong at [[Bilbringi system/Legends|Bilbringi]] and incarcerated in a Yuuzhan Vong prison camp on the planet [[Selvaris]]. Thorsh became the de facto leader of a group of prisoners who planned and dug a tunnel to escape; he went by the codename "Garban." Fellow prisoners, Humans [[Pash Cracken/Legends|Pash Cracken]] and [[Judder Page/Legends|Judder Page]], had Thorsh and three [[Bith/Legends|Bith]] inmates memorize a mathematical equation on a [[holowafer]] so that the [[Alien/Legends|non-Humans]] could smuggle the information out past the guards. During the escape attempt, Thorsh reached freedom and fled on a [[Swoop/Legends|swoop]], but the Bith were killed. Thorsh rendezvoused with the New Republic [[Freighter/Legends|freighter]] [[Millennium Falcon/Legends|''Millennium Falcon'']] and escaped to the planet [[Contruum/Legends|Contruum]] to debrief [[General/Legends|General]] [[Airen Cracken/Legends|Airen Cracken]] on the information from the holowafer.<ref name="TUF" />

Some Jenets could [[Force-sensitive/Legends|manipulate]] the Force. One of these was the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Grand Master/Legends|Grand Master]] [[Fae Coven]], who lived during the [[New Sith Wars]] and helped write ''[[The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force]]''.<ref name="TJP" /><ref name="TFN Wallace">{{JCFCite|url=posts/31329847|board=Literature|thread=The Jedi Path. (Now you too can actually pretend with slightly more accuracy that you're a Jedi!)|user=[[Daniel Wallace|Dan_Wallace]]|date=2010-10-25|time=1:50 PM|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20180609035645/http://boards.theforce.net/threads/the-jedi-path-now-you-too-can-actually-pretend-with-slightly-more-accuracy-that-youre-a-jedi.31091974/page-9}}</ref> Centuries later, the Jenet [[Reeqo Swen]] also [[Jedi training/Legends|studied]] to be a Jedi. While still an [[Padawan/Legends|apprentice]] in [[43 ABY]], Swen served as a guard at the [[New Jedi Temple]] on Coruscant, when Han Solo turned over the prisoner [[Yaqeel Saav'etu]] to the Jedi.The Jenet and his partner, the [[Duros/Legends|Duros]] [[Melari Ruxon]], both resigned from the [[New Jedi Order|Jedi Order]] in protest over the political policies of [[Natasi Daala]], the Galactic Alliance Chief of State. The move spooked Daala, who feared the consequences of allowing Jedi&mdash;or former Jedi&mdash;to become independent of the central government.<ref name="A" />

==Behind the scenes==
Author [[Troy Denning]] introduced the Jenets in the book ''[[Galaxy Guide 4: Alien Races]]'', published in [[1989]] as part of ''[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game]]'' from [[West End Games]]. The book provides statistics to allow players to portray Jenet characters; they are described as more dexterous and perceptive than Humans, but deficient in intelligence, [[Pilot/Legends|piloting]] potential, physical strength, and technical prowess.<ref name="GG4a" /> The species' background was later expanded slightly by [[Chuck Truett]] for the book's [[Galaxy Guide 4: Alien Races (Second Edition)|second edition]], published in [[1994]]. Their revised statistics bring them more into line with other species, with only a deficit in technical aptitude. They receive bonuses when climbing, listening, and swimming, and they gain extra skills due to their eidetic memories. They can also fit through small openings.<ref name="GG4b" /> An entry in the 1994 [[Roleplaying game|gaming]] supplement ''[[Creatures of the Galaxy]]'' details another chapter of the Jenets' history&mdash;their early battles and conquest of the danchaf. The danchaf creature and its relationship to Garban's sentient rodents was designed by [[Phil Brucato]].<ref name="COTG" /> Jenets have since featured in various minor roles in ''[[Star Wars]]'' fiction.

With the release of ''[[Ultimate Alien Anthology]]'' in [[2003]], the species was adapted to the ''[[Star Wars Roleplaying Game]]'' from [[Wizards of the Coast]]. Their statistics for this system make Jenets deficient in their physical power, agility, and intelligence, and much lower in their likability in comparison to Humans. However, they receive the ability to remember everything they see or hear, as well as bonuses to climbing, escaping bonds, jumping, and swimming.<ref name="UAA" />

Sources disagree about the age of maturity for the species. According to both editions of ''Galaxy Guide 4: Alien Races'',<ref name="GG4s">''[[Galaxy Guide 4: Alien Races]]''; [[Galaxy Guide 4: Alien Races (Second Edition)|''Galaxy Guide 4: Alien Races'', Second Edition]]</ref> and [[The Essential Guide to Alien Species (real-world book)|''The Essential Guide to Alien Species'']], Jenets are mature at one standard year of age.<ref name="EGAS" /> However, ''Ultimate Alien Anthology'' makes this nine standard years.<ref name="UAA" /> This article follows the more recent source, as it was published last.
